description.narrative:
Africa has been eared marked, by large international oil and gas corporations, and national oil and gas corporations to explore, develop, export and industrialise the oil and gas sector in Africa. The industrialisation of the oil and gas sector in Africais centred around extracting and exporting oil and gas to countries outside of Africa, developing the energy sector in Africa and locking Africa into the use of oil and gas as its main natural resources for the development of the energy sector.
As a result, various key drivers are being implemented. At this present stage, there are policy developments that are facilitating oil and gas explorations andfossil fuel power stations, direct foreign investments being made to construct and develop the oil andgas sector, contractual agreements between governments and oil and gas corporations being signed to sell the resource, actual construction of oil and gas pipelines and rigs to extract the oil and gas, the development and construction of gas-to-power electricity stations and the development ofdiesel turbine electricity stations.
Despite this drive to lock Africa’s reliance on the fossil fuel industry, there are few centralised resources or matrix toolkits that allow communities, people of interest, activists, international organisations, local NGOs, lawyers and regional NGOs to access critical information around the financing oil and gas projects, changing policy for oil and gas development, which corporation is extracting the oil or gas, which companyis constructing power stations or the contractual deals that exist allowing for such development to occur.
In light of the above, the project's main outcome is to create a live digital map showing details of fossil fuel projects and clean energy projects across Africa that consider the impact and effect of such projectsat various levels. This project, however, will have to be split into two phases. The first phase, which is directly linked to this grant, will be around the scoping and design of thematrix toolkit. It is critical that the various key partners working on this project get a lay of the land after which the live digital map can be designed and developed. Once that has been completed the project will then move us into phase two.

participating-org.narrative:
Natural Justice is part of Consortium with the Pan-African Climate Justice Alliance, Oxfam-Novib and FEMNET, which has applied for a partnership with the Ministry of The Netherlands under the Power of Voices. We will be notified of its success on the 1stof May 2021. In the case it is successful, the financial flows will go directly between PACJA and Natural Justice; Oxfam Novib is out of thisequation – which is one of the conditions for funding this proposal.
The project aims to support indigenous peoples and local communities and their grassroots organisations in up to seven countries in Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, DRC, Nigeria, Senegal, Uganda and Madagascar) in their efforts to resist and be protected against such threats as they defend their collective lands and territories oflife. The actions and forms of support will be both defensive and preventative in nature and will respond directly to their self-determined needs and priorities, including, inter alia, awareness campaigns, trainings, digitaland physical security measures, legal support, and communications platforms for regional and global advocacy. The project relates most closely to the impact themes of “improved access to resources and employment” and “open up spaces for political participation and to promote citizen engagement”. For the former, the project supports indigenous peoples and local communities to remain on their customary lands and territories and continue their self-determined ways of life and livelihoods. For the latter, the project supports indigenous peoples and communities, especially those who are routinely marginalised and discriminated against and face multiple intersectional inequalities, to advocate for legal and political recognition for their contributions to conservation and sustainable development and for their rights and collective responsibilities to defend their lands and territories.
Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment, a not-for-profit organisation registered in South Africa and Kenya with hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, is the project applicant and passes the online eligibility test. The project will be undertaken by grassroots organisations in up to seven countries in Africa with focused support within the region from Natural Justice and local/regional and global support from the ICCA Consortium, a non-for-profit association registered in Switzerland with more than 175 Member organisations in 80 countries, including Natural Justice.
The project is based on mini proposalsprepared by grassroots organisations about specific situations and priority actions of indigenous peoples’ and communities’ territories of life and their defenders under threat. These include local and national plans for the projected 2020 global mobilisation on land and environmental defenders (2-9 December 2020), which provides an important and timely opportunity to advocate for their rights through local-to-global collective action. Their plans also outline priority actions to build momentum towardsthis global mobilisation and address emerging threats that may arise thereafter. Importantly, whereas many campaigns on environmental and human rights defenders focus solely on individuals, this project will include a strong focus on collective communityandintersectional dimensions of defenders’ work. The proposed timeline is May 2021 - April 2022 and the requested budget is EUR 200,000. The project will also build on the African Environmental Defenders Fund implemented by Natural Justice in partnership with the International Land Coalition (ILC) and the ICCA Consortium, bringing in further synergies and opportunities for collective local-regional-global action.
The goal is to minimise and manage the risks faced by Environmental and Land Rights Defendersin Africa by standing with them in solidarity through increased support to enhance their resilience in terms of protection and increased visibility of the struggle of Defenders.
